question: How does the SHIPPED model behave on generator regimes it was never fitted to, with nothing retuned afterwards?
no_retuning: No generator parameter was adjusted after seeing any result below, and no threshold was re-derived. The artefact is the one the cockpit ships.

artefact.note: Trained by validation/experiments/artefact.py with the exporter's own CAT/DROP/split/hyperparameters, imported rather than restated. `reproduces_shipped_thresholds` records whether this fit lands on the same operating point the committed export shipped; a False there means the two have diverged and every experiment below is describing a different model from the one in the cockpit.

control_band_note: the range spanned by three development-parameter panels differing only in generator seed. A regime inside this range has moved a metric no further than the seed alone does.

unseen_seed.why: the control: how much does a metric move when NOTHING but the seed changes? A regime that moves a number less than this has shown nothing.

cox_served.reading: under-confident: the score spreads risk narrower than the outcomes do

simulated_cost.label: SIMULATION RESULT at the frozen operating point, on a synthetic book
simulated_cost.caveat: Not a projected bank saving. Every cost parameter is an ASSUMPTION (src/costs.py PARAM_NOTES); the book is synthetic; and the regime's own parameters are deliberately outside the development setting. Compare regimes to each other, never read the absolute figure as rupees the bank would keep.

unseen_seed_b.why: a second control. One control gives a point; three give a BAND, and without that band no single-seed regime difference below is readable.

macro_shock.mechanism: risk_intercept -1.75 + abrupt onset + 3x statement gaps, together
macro_shock.why: a compound downturn: more borrowers go bad, they go bad faster, and the data feed degrades at the same time — which is what actually happens in a shock.
